rows.label: Cleopatra
rows.description: Queen of Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt from 51 to 30 BCE
rows.hook: allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, and is said to have died from a snake bite

rows.label: Alexander the Great
rows.description: king of Macedonia and conqueror of Achaemenid Persia (356–323 BC)
rows.hook: conquered a vast empire stretching to India and died young in Babylon

rows.label: Tutankhamun
rows.description: 14th century BCE (18th dynasty) Egyptian pharaoh
rows.hook: was a boy king whose nearly intact tomb was found by Howard Carter, full of golden treasure

rows.label: Ramesses II
rows.description: Egyptian third pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty
rows.hook: ruled for over sixty years, fought the Hittites at Kadesh and built the temples of Abu Simbel

rows.label: Xerxes I
rows.description: fifth Achaemenid emperor (486–465 BC)
rows.hook: led a huge Persian invasion of Greece and was defeated at the naval battle of Salamis

rows.label: Akhenaten
rows.description: Egyptian pharaoh in 18th Dynasty
rows.hook: abandoned the old gods to worship a single sun disk and moved the capital to a new city

rows.label: Nefertiti
rows.description: Egyptian queen and Great Royal Wife (chief consort) of Akhenaten, an Egyptian Pharaoh
rows.hook: is remembered for a famous painted limestone bust displayed in a Berlin museum

rows.label: Caesarion
rows.description: last pharaoh of Ptolemaic Egypt from 44 to 30 BC
rows.hook: was the young son of Julius Caesar and a famous queen and was the last of the pharaohs

rows.label: Darius I
rows.description: The fourth and greatest Achaemenid emperor (522–486 BC)
rows.hook: expanded the Persian Empire, built Persepolis and sent an army that lost at Marathon

rows.label: Hatshepsut
rows.description: 5th Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt (c. 1479 BC - 1458 BC)
rows.hook: was a woman who ruled as pharaoh, often shown wearing a false beard

rows.label: Ptolemy I Soter
rows.description: Macedonian general, ruler of Egypt
rows.hook: was a general under Alexander the Great who seized the Nile kingdom and founded a long royal line

rows.label: Narmer
rows.description: ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the Early Dynastic Period
rows.hook: is traditionally credited with uniting Upper and Lower lands under one crown

rows.label: Khufu
rows.description: Fourth Dynasty ancient Egyptian pharaoh
rows.hook: built the Great Pyramid of Giza, the largest of the pyramids

rows.label: Seti I
rows.description: second pharaoh of Ancient Egypt's 19th dynasty
rows.hook: built a magnificent tomb in the Valley of the Kings and was the father of Ramesses the Great

rows.label: Thutmose III
rows.description: sixth Egyptian Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty
rows.hook: was a warrior pharaoh who won the Battle of Megiddo and is called the Napoleon of ancient times

rows.label: Darius III
rows.description: last king of the Achaemenid Empire (r. 336–330 BC)
rows.hook: was the Persian king defeated by Alexander the Great at Gaugamela and Issus

rows.label: Amenhotep III
rows.description: ninth Pharaoh of the Eighteenth dynasty of Egypt
rows.hook: ruled at the peak of the kingdom's wealth and built the Colossi of Memnon

rows.label: Ramesses I
rows.description: founding pharaoh of Ancient Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty
rows.hook: founded a royal line but ruled for only about a year or two, leaving his son to build the glory

rows.label: Ramesses III
rows.description: Egyptian pharaoh of the 20th dynasty
rows.hook: was the last great warrior pharaoh, who repelled the Sea Peoples and survived a harem conspiracy

rows.label: Cambyses II
rows.description: The second Achaemenid emperor (530–522 BC)
rows.hook: led the Persian conquest of the Nile kingdom and was the son of Cyrus the Great
